DT_Checkpoint9.text: CHECKPOINT 9 — Busy Stack transit entrance built from older concrete and newer municipal retrofit layers. Body-specific scanner frames, access barriers, civic decals, route signage and ordinary commuter clutter make classification feel like routine infrastructure rather than a military border. Mixed Baselines, Augments and Organics share the same circulation space but do not move through it with equal friction.

DT_Overpass.text: ELEVATED OVERPASS / CONCOURSE — Aging heavy-traffic structure layered above transit and pedestrian circulation. Exposed repair history, reinforced joints, newer composite patches over old concrete, service access and clearly readable load paths should make structural action physically understandable. The space is public and heavily used, not an abandoned industrial ruin.

DT_OversightOffice.text: OVERSIGHT OFFICE — Cleaner, colder governance-level municipal workspace: controlled access, glass partitions, orderly records, surveillance and incident feeds, restrained civic finishes and generous space compared with lower Stack workplaces. New administrative surfaces sit over older civic bones. Authority should look effortless and procedural rather than sinister.

DT_AugmentClinic.text: AUGMENT CLINIC — Busy converted parking/service-level medical and calibration workspace built into old concrete. Practical diagnostic rigs, alignment fixtures, repair benches and worn clinical equipment serve patients with visibly different qualities and costs of augmentation. Body maintenance is ordinary healthcare and class is visible in the finish, age and integration of hardware; avoid chrome cyberpunk spectacle.

DT_OrganicSafehouse.text: ORGANIC RESIDENTIAL / REPAIR SPACE — Humid inhabited service-volume neighborhood and workshop with direct infrastructure access, repair benches, shared work surfaces, personal belongings and ordinary domestic life. Organic bodies are maintained here without turning the environment into a laboratory or machinery warren. The place is culturally owned and lived in, not a hidden sewer refuge.

DT_DataCore.text: CIVIC DATA CORE — Quiet machine-native analysis environment inside the Stack's administrative infrastructure. Controlled black, white and cool luminous information surfaces, physical civic hardware and precise spatial organization support simultaneous system-scale reasoning. It should feel functional and institutional, not like a villain lair, hologram spectacle or magical cyberspace.

DT_TransitSpine.text: UNDERCITY TRANSIT / SERVICE SPINE — Layered maintenance route carrying rail, power, structural and civic systems beneath public levels. Old concrete, newer composite reinforcement, conduits, service walkways, access gates and active machinery reveal decades of accumulated construction. Geography, exits and load-bearing systems must remain visually legible during action.

DT_WhiteFacility.text: WHITE FACILITY — Immaculate unmarked controlled site embedded inside ordinary municipal infrastructure. Seamless pale surfaces, precise interfaces, concealed access and conspicuous maintenance perfection contrast with the accumulated Stack around it. Keep it bureaucratically plausible and physically real rather than futuristic mysticism.

DT_SharedDistrictRooftop.text: SHARED-DISTRICT ROOFTOP / SERVICE LEVEL — Exposed civic layer overlooking the accumulated vertical Stack: old structures, retrofits, transit arteries, residential pockets, public projections, service equipment and governance towers occupy the same skyline. Mixed-category everyday life should remain visible below the political spectacle.

DT_Concourse17.text: CONCOURSE 17 — Desirable three-level middle-Stack commercial and transit concourse built through an older structural bay. Shops, food counters, clinics, pedestrian bridges, public seating and transit connections wrap a tall central volume with visible service doors and suppression hardware. The district has a strong Organic commercial presence but remains genuinely mixed: Baselines, Augments and Organics shop and commute here together. Organic accommodations are normalized into some storefronts and public fixtures rather than turning the place into a special enclave. Maintain clear geography across the incident: central atrium, upper bridge, primary exits, compartment partitions, secondary service route and ceiling suppression grid must stay spatially consistent from Pages 1–11.

DT_PublicHearingChamber.text: PUBLIC HEARING CHAMBER — Formal governance-level civic room designed to make procedure look fair: broad public gallery, accessible witness table, officials on a shallow raised dais, integrated evidence displays, press positions and visible security kept at the edges. Materials are expensive but restrained, with daylight or soft civic illumination rather than theatrical darkness. Mixed-category attendance should be visible. The architecture gives everyone a place to speak while the institutional control of agenda, framing, camera angles and official record remains visually obvious.

DT_HearingMediaCorridor.text: HEARING MEDIA / SERVICE CORRIDOR — Transitional space immediately outside the public chamber where polished civic architecture meets press staging, staff access and service circulation. Camera crews, statement screens, badge-controlled doors and quieter side alcoves allow public testimony to become edited media language within meters of the room where it was spoken. Use the same materials and signage family as the hearing chamber so Pages 14–16 read as one continuous political event.

DT_CivicVerificationGate.text: CIVIC VERIFICATION GATE — Ordinary transit/civic access point retrofitted after the emergency order. Existing human circulation remains mostly unchanged while new capability-verification scanners, secondary queue rails, function-permission displays and polite public-safety signage have been added beside it. The retrofit should look temporary, modular and administratively reasonable, not like a prison checkpoint. Its politics are visible in unequal friction: Baseline and most Augment commuters keep moving while Organics are diverted into slower review paths.

DT_OrganicCommunityHall.text: ORGANIC COMMUNITY HALL — Multipurpose neighborhood room adapted by residents rather than designed by government: reinforced mixed-height seating, varied body clearances, repair-safe surfaces, humidity zoning, community notices, food and personal objects coexist with ordinary meeting equipment. The room should support disagreement, mutual aid and mundane local politics. It is neither a revolutionary bunker nor a factory floor. Mixed economic circumstances and different Organic lots/functions remain visible.

DT_PermitOffice.text: MUNICIPAL PERMIT OFFICE — Busy civic-service floor occupying an older Stack structural volume behind a cleaner public frontage. Queue lanes, numbered counters, body-aware scanners, records terminals, document printers, seal stations and staff workrooms make administration physical and legible. The new Organic capability order has been layered onto existing systems, producing improvised signs, contradictory fields and growing lines rather than a purpose-built oppression machine. Axiom's intervention should visibly reduce queue chaos without making the office futuristic or frictionless.
